item.title: Why is Trump rolling out the red carpet for China's Xi?
item.description:
President Donald Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to Washington, D.C., on Wednesday, just two months after accusing Beijing of interfering in U.S. elections during a prime-time address. Xi was personally greeted by Trump at Joint Base Andrews with the help of two B-1 bombers that soared overhead after the Chinese president stepped off the plane. The visit is expected to include bilateral talks and a state dinner, with trade, artificial intelligence, national security, Taiwan, and the war in Iran among the issues likely to be discussed. This is the second meeting between the two leaders this year, following Trump’s visit to China in May. The timing puts a series of unresolved disputes between Washington and Beijing in the spotlight alongside a high-profile diplomatic meeting. The two countries are still negotiating trade issues, including rare-earth exports and technology…

item.title: Hurricane Polo brings fears of heavy rain and landslides in Mexico
item.description:
Hurricane Polo intensifying in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Mexico on Monday, Sept. 21, 2026. —NOAA/AP Hurricane Polo has become one of the strongest hurricanes ever recorded in the western hemisphere. Polo, off the Pacific coast of Mexico, evolved from a weak tropical storm to a Category 5 hurricane on Tuesday. Category 5 hurricanes, the most powerful level on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale, are rare, although rising ocean temperatures have made them more frequent in recent years . The hurricane was drifting northeast at 1 mile per hour in the eastern Pacific Ocean on Tuesday night, about 210 miles south of Zihuatanejo, Mexico. Forecasters expect it to begin turning northwest, and move west-northwestward near the Mexican coastline over the next few days, with its core remaining offshore. item.title: A Trump Appointee Blocks the President's Banishment of Disfavored News Outlets
item.description:
This morning, a federal judge in the District of Columbia temporarily blocked President Donald Trump's attempt to ban CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House, ordering restoration of the "hard passes" held by employees of those news outlets. U.S. District Judge Timothy J. Kelly, a Trump appointee, said the sudden banishment of CNN et al., which the president announced last Friday, seemed inconsistent with the due process required by D.C. Circuit precedents, and he expressed appropriate skepticism about the post-hoc national security rationale for that precipitous decision. In addition to their due process claims, CNN et al. argued that their exclusion unconstitutionally discriminated against them based on viewpoint and retaliated against them for protected speech. item.title: Why are Ireland vs Israel football matches so controversial?
item.description:
Ireland and Israel are, at least for now, set for some really weird soccer matches. Unfriendlies, you might say. Their national men’s teams have a home-and-home series scheduled to open this weekend, only there are no home games for either side. Both matches will be played in Central Europe: one in an empty stadium, the other with only Israeli fans. The top story in Ireland these days, sports or otherwise, is that the games will be played at all. “I think we all agree we shouldn’t be in the position where we have to play the game,” John Martin, head of the Football Association of Ireland (FAI), said last week. And Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson said he’d personally polled all his players, and "none of us feel comfortable playing in these games."

item.title: Police arrest far-right activist Daniel Thomas after ‘dinghy slashed in Channel’
item.description:
Thirty-seven-year-old in custody on suspicion of crimes including criminal damage with intent to endanger life The far-right agitator and anti-migrant activist Daniel Thomas has been arrested on suspicion of “criminal damage with intent to endanger life”, after he filmed himself appearing to slash the side of a dinghy in the middle of the Channel while a rescuer was onboard. The arrest came as the Home Office recorded 781 arrivals in 10 boats on Wednesday, the highest number for a single day so far this year. Responding to the figures, the government said it would “push further and harder” to crack down on the people organising the crossings. Continue reading...
